predecessors.name: Kingdom of Ava
predecessors.text: Toungoo and Kyaukse, the Toungoo core

successors.name: Restored Hanthawaddy Kingdom
successors.text: the Toungoo realm at its end: Ava and its country, sacked on 22 March 1752 by the Mon armies of Pegu, with Lower Burma already Mon since 1740

successors.name: Konbaung dynasty
successors.text: Upper Burma north of Ava, reconquered by Aung Zeya (Alaungpaya) by December 1752; Ava itself fell to him a year later

ledger.x: 1502: Mingyi Nyo's Toungoo, de facto independent of Ava since 1501, holds Kyaukse.
Late 1538: Toungoo takes Pegu.
1539: Tabinshwehti moves the capital from Toungoo to Pegu ('In 1539, Tabinshwehti moved the capital to Pegu'; infobox 'Pegu (Bago) (1539-1599)').
1539: the Irrawaddy delta.
November 1540: a Toungoo force attacks Martaban.
Late 1541: Toungoo besieges Prome, which had sheltered fleeing Hanthawaddy troops in 1539.
May 1541: Martaban falls and the Mon south submits.
May 1541: Martaban falls.
19 May 1542: Prome surrenders.
19 May 1542: Toungoo annexes Prome.
1544: Tabinshwehti takes Pagan and is crowned there.
28 October 1546: Toungoo invades Arakan.
Late 1547: Saw Lagun Ein is sent against the Siamese at Ye and Tavoy.
30 January 1547: truce with Min Bin.
February 1549: the Burmese retreat from Siam.
30 April 1550: Tabinshwehti is assassinated and his governors rebel.
May 1550: Prome revolts.
ledger.cp: Prome revolt of Thado Dhamma Yaza I

ledger.x: August 1551: Bayinnaung crushes the Prome revolt.
ledger.cp: Prome revolt of Thado Dhamma Yaza I

ledger.x: 1552: the empire is whole again.
22 January 1555: Bayinnaung takes Ava and Upper Burma.
January 1557: Bayinnaung invades the Shan country.
March 1557: the cis-Salween Shan states fall.
March 1557: the fighting in the Shan country ends with most of the cis-Salween states in Toungoo hands.
November 1557: Mone, Nyaungshwe and Mobye fall.
2 April 1558: Chiang Mai submits and Lan Na becomes a tributary.
February 1560: Manipur submits.
16 December 1562: Kengtung submits.
March-April 1563: the Chinese Shan states of the Taping valley.
December 1563: Toungoo's armies take Kamphaeng Phet.
18 February 1564: Ayutthaya surrenders.
18 February 1564: Siam's western strip passes to Toungoo.
18 February 1564: Mahinthrathirat is installed as Siam's vassal king.
25 November 1564: Chiang Mai falls again and Lan Na passes to a Burmese-appointed ruler.
November 1564: the same tributary state continues as lan-na.
2 January 1565: Burmese armies take Vientiane.
1 August 1565: the Burmese leave Vientiane.
1568: Siam revolts.
1568: war with Siam.
2 August 1569: Ayutthaya falls again.
September 1569: Maha Thammarachathirat is made Siam's vassal king.
February 1570: Burmese troops hold Vientiane after Setthathirath leaves it.
April 1570: Bayinnaung gives up.
July 1571: Mohnyin and Mogaung revolt.
December 1574: Lan Xang becomes a Burmese vassal kingdom, not an annexed province.
6 December 1574: Burmese armies enter Vientiane unopposed.
16 April 1575: the Burmese king returns to Pegu.
1576: Mohnyin and Mogaung are brought back.
November 1580: the Burmese fleet occupies Sandoway.
1581: the invasion is called off.
1584: Siam is independent again.
December 1586: a Burmese army reaches Ayutthaya.
20 April 1587: the Burmese withdraw after heavy losses, a Siamese victory (Burmese-Siamese War (1584-1593) page).
1591: Lan Xang casts off Burmese allegiance.
Late December 1592: the Burmese reach Suphan Buri.
1593: Manipur leaves the empire.
Early 1593: Siam takes the Tenasserim coast.
January 1593: the Burmese retreat with heavy casualties after the single combat at Nong Sarai (8 January 1593 in Burmese chronicles, 18 January in Siamese ones; Burmese-Siamese War (1584-1593) page).
1594: the Mon provinces go to Siam.
1596: Lan Na leaves.
1597: the other vassals are gone.
1597: the Chinese Shan states are gone with the other vassals.
1597: the Shan states and the Kachin hills break away.
ledger.cp: Shan states and other former vassals

ledger.x: 1599: Lower Burma is lost to rival lords.
ledger.cp: Lower Burma lords: Toungoo, Prome, Syriam and Arakan

ledger.x: 19 December 1599: the First Toungoo Empire falls and the dynasty continues at Ava.
1599: the seat is Ava.
1600: Siam invades Lower Burma.
1600: Naresuan gives up.
July 1608: Anaukpetlun takes Prome.
1610: Anaukpetlun takes Toungoo.
1613: Anaukpetlun takes Syriam.
1613: Martaban and Tavoy.
1613: Anaukpetlun attacks the Siamese.
1614: Lan Na is Burmese again.
1617: Anaukpetlun makes Bago his capital and is crowned King of Bago that year.
1618: Burma and Siam agree.
1628: Lan Na is independent again.
1631: Lan Na is Burma's tributary for the third time.
1634: Thalun moves the capital to Ava ('Thalun was compelled to relocate the capital to Ava in 1634').
1653: the northern Shan states and the Kachin hills are inside Cliopatria's shape again.
ledger.cp: northern Shan states and Kachin hills

ledger.x: November 1663: Narai invades Burma.
May 1664: the Siamese withdraw.
1727: Chiang Mai revolts and Lan Na is lost.
About 1738: the northern Shan states and the Kachin hills leave Cliopatria's shape.
ledger.cp: northern Shan states and Kachin hills

ledger.x: 29 November 1740: Pegu rises and Lower Burma is lost.
1745: Prome and Toungoo fall to the Mons.
November 1751: Pegu invades Upper Burma.
22 March 1752: Ava falls.
22 March 1752: the Mons take Ava and Upper Burma.
22 March 1752: the Toungoo dynasty ends at Ava.

wars.name: Toungoo-Hanthawaddy War
wars.outcome: Toungoo conquers Hanthawaddy: Pegu in late 1538 or early 1539, the delta by 1539, Martaban in May 1541; Prome falls on 19 May 1542.

wars.name: Toungoo conquest of the Pagan country
wars.outcome: Tabinshwehti takes Pagan from the Confederation of Shan States and is crowned there in 1544.

wars.name: Toungoo invasion of Arakan
wars.outcome: The invasion of 28 October 1546 reached Launggyet in January 1547 and ended in a truce on 30 January 1547; no Arakanese land is annexed.

wars.name: Burmese-Siamese War (1547-1549)
wars.outcome: The Burmese invasion of Siam (14 October 1548) fails: the siege is broken in January 1549 and the Burmese retreat in February 1549 in exchange for captive nobles.

wars.name: Rebellion of the governors after Tabinshwehti
wars.outcome: The empire falls apart on 30 April 1550; Prome revolts in May 1550 and is put down in August 1551; Bayinnaung reunifies the kingdom within two years.

wars.name: Toungoo conquest of Ava and the Shan states
wars.outcome: Ava falls on 22 January 1555; most of the cis-Salween Shan states are Toungoo's by March 1557 and Mone, Nyaungshwe and Mobye in November 1557.

wars.name: Toungoo conquest of Lan Na, Manipur and the trans-Salween Shan states
wars.outcome: Lan Na submits on 2 April 1558, Manipur around February 1560, Kengtung before 16 December 1562, the Taping valley in March-April 1563: all tributaries.

wars.name: Burmese-Siamese War (1563-1564)
wars.outcome: Five armies leave Pegu on 1 November 1563, take Kamphaeng Phet on 4 December and Ayutthaya surrenders on 18 February 1564; Mahinthrathirat becomes the vassal king.

wars.name: Burmese-Lao War (1565-1575)
wars.outcome: Vientiane taken on 2 January 1565 and left on 1 August 1565; Burmese troops hold it again from February to April 1570; entered unopposed on 6 December 1574, Maha Oupahat made king of a vassal Lan Xang and the Burmese king back at Pegu on 16 April 1575.

wars.name: Burmese-Siamese War (1568-1569)
wars.outcome: Siam revolts in 1568; Ayutthaya falls on 2 August 1569 and Maha Thammarachathirat is made vassal king in September 1569.

wars.name: Mohnyin and Mogaung revolts
wars.outcome: The two hill states revolt in July 1571 and again in 1574; the Mohnyin saopha is killed in 1575 and Mogaung is restored in 1576 (the Mogaung saopha before the king on 30 September 1577).

wars.name: Toungoo invasion of Arakan (1580-1581)
wars.outcome: A Burmese fleet sails on 15 October 1580 and occupies Sandoway in November; the invasion is called off when Bayinnaung dies in October 1581.

wars.name: Burmese-Siamese wars (1584-1593)
wars.outcome: Five punitive Burmese campaigns fail: Siam is independent from 3 May 1584, the Burmese reach Ayutthaya (December 1586 to April 1587) and Suphan Buri (December 1592 to January 1593) and are driven back; Siam then takes the Tenasserim coast in early 1593 and…

wars.name: Collapse of the Toungoo Empire
wars.outcome: Siam seizes the Tenasserim coast in 1595; the vassals break away by 1597; Prome and Toungoo jointly invade Lower Burma in 1598 and capture Pegu in 1599; the empire falls on 19 December 1599 and Siam invades Lower Burma in 1600.

wars.name: Nyaungyan and Anaukpetlun's reunification
wars.outcome: Prome retaken in 1608, Toungoo in 1610, Syriam in 1613, Martaban and Tavoy in 1613, Lan Na in 1614; the 1618 agreement leaves Mottama to Burma and Chiang Mai to Siam (Anaukpetlun page).

wars.name: Burmese-Siamese War (1662-1664)
wars.outcome: Burmese defensive victory: Siam takes Chiang Mai in February 1663 and gives it up later that year; the three-pronged invasion of November 1663 is withdrawn in May 1664.

wars.name: Chiang Mai revolt against Burma
wars.outcome: The Burmese army is driven back in 1727-1728 and 1731-1732; Chiang Mai and the Ping valley are independent until 1757.

wars.name: Mon revolt and the fall of Ava
wars.outcome: Pegu rises on 29 November 1740; the Mons hold Prome from 1745; Ava is sacked on 22 March 1752 and the Toungoo dynasty ends.

certainty.note: The pages give no treaty or survey frontier for any period.
